questions.q: Which shortcut key combination is used to **bold** selected text in MS Word?
questions.x: Ctrl + B is the standard shortcut to toggle bold formatting in MS Word.

questions.q: What is the default file extension for a **Microsoft Excel 2010** worksheet?
questions.x: Microsoft Excel 2010 uses **.xlsx** as the default file extension for open XML-based workbooks.

questions.q: Which file format is primarily used for **high-quality, lossless** image compression?
questions.x: **.png** supports lossless compression and is ideal for high-quality images, including transparency.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key to **rename** a selected file/folder in Windows Explorer?
questions.x: Pressing **F2** allows you to rename a selected file or folder in Windows.

questions.q: Which of the following is a **vector graphics** file format?
questions.x: **.svg** (Scalable Vector Graphics) is a vector format, unlike raster formats like JPEG or TIFF.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key to **create a new folder** in Windows File Explorer?
questions.x: **Ctrl + Shift + N** creates a new folder in Windows File Explorer.

questions.q: Which file extension is used for **compressed archive** files in Windows?
questions.x: **.zip** is the most common compressed archive format natively supported by Windows.

questions.q: What is the shortcut key to **select all** items in a folder in Windows?
questions.x: **Ctrl + A** universally selects all items in a folder or document.

questions.q: Which of the following is the binary equivalent of the decimal number 19?
questions.x: The decimal number 19 converts to binary as 10011 (16 + 2 + 1).

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal (base-16) representation of the binary number 111010?
questions.x: Binary 111010 equals 58 in decimal, which is 3A in hexadecimal.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid octal digit?
questions.x: Octal digits range from 0 to 7, so 8 is invalid.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation 'ROM' stand for in computer memory terminology?
questions.x: ROM (Read-Only Memory) stores permanent data that cannot be altered.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct binary representation of the hexadecimal number '2F'?
The abbreviation 'LAN' refers to which type of network?
questions.x: LAN (Local Area Network) connects devices within a limited area like a home or office.
